paper_metadata.title: An ambient ductile TiHfVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy: Cold rolling, mechanical properties, lattice distortion, and first-principles prediction

evidence.quote: In this work, an ambient ductility TiHfVNbTa alloy was prepared, and its microstructure, mechanical properties, phase stability, lattice distortion, and basic physical properties were investigated by combing experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
the lattice distortion of TiHfVNbTa is quantitatively analyzed by comparing the distorted and undistorted configurations from DFT calculations.

The cold rolling experiments reveal that TiHfVNbTa exhibits excellent malleability, and on crack formation under the 84% thickness reduction.
In order to eliminate the cold work hardening and residual stress induced by the rolling process, the 84% rolled sample was annealed at 1200 °C for 45 min.
Moreover, the structural stability, lattice distortion, mechanical, and electronic properties of TiHfVNbTa alloy were discussed based on the density functional theory (DFT) calculations.

The button ingots of equiatomic TiHfVNbTa alloy were melted by vacuum arc furnace with high purity ( > 99.95%) metal elements within a Ti-gettered ultra-high purity argon ( > 99.99%) atmosphere.
As show in Fig. 1 , the ingots were rolled into a sheet (with 84% thickness reduction).
The dog-bone specimens were annealed at temperatures of 1200 °C for times of 45 min in evacuated quartz tube with 5 × 10^3 torr to acquire equiaxed microstructures.

All DFT calculations are performed by using the VASP code [ 20 ] with the plane-wave projector augmented wave (PAW) [ 21 ] method to describe the ion electron interaction, and the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) [ 22 ] to treat the exchange-correlation function.
